bandReport.notes: Band complete: p13 (printed 29) Q77-80, p14 (31) Q81-82, p15 (33) Q83-84, p16 (35) Q85-86. Six questions per page-pair earlier in the paper drops to four then two here because Q81 onward are full-page data-sufficiency items. NO Directions blocks and NO figures anywhere in p13-p16 — verified by reading every page at full resolution; no question refers to a diagram, and there are no data tables. SEAMS BOTH CLEAN: p12 (printed 27) ends with Q76 complete (options (a)-(d) all printed on that page), and p17 (printed 37) opens with Q87, a fresh self-contained item — nothing straddles either boundary and no question is stranded. Q81-Q86 are NOT a Directions set: each one reprints its own 'A Question is given followed by two Statements I and II' preamble in full, so each is self-contained and carries no shared context/setLabel (same treatment as 2024-2 Q61). The four option texts are identical across all six of them, which is the printed paper, not a copy-paste slip. NOTE the (d) wording here is 'can be answered even without using any of the Statements' — it differs from the 2024-2 paper's (d) 'cannot be answered even by using both the Statements together'; transcribed as printed. Printed page numbers run odd-only (27, 29, 31, 33, 35, 37): the even pages are the Hindi translation and are not in the render.

questions.stem: A conical tent has an angle of \(60^\circ\) at the vertex. If the curved surface area is \(100\) m\(^2\), then what is the volume of the tent?
A right circular cone and a hemisphere have equal base and equal volume. What is the ratio of the height of the cone to the radius of the hemisphere?
A wire is in the form of an equilateral triangle with an area of \(36\sqrt{3}\) cm\(^2\). If it is changed into a semicircle, then what is its radius?

options.label: A
options.text: \(\frac{9}{\pi}\) cm

options.label: C
options.text: \(\frac{18}{\pi}\) cm

options.label: D
options.text: None of the above

questions.stem: Let the area of the largest possible square inscribed in a circle of unit radius be \(x\). Let the area of the largest possible circle inscribed in a square of unit side length be \(y\). What is the relation between \(x\) and \(y\)?

A Question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements.

Question :

What is the remainder when \(x^{2n} - y^{2n} + 1\) is divided by \(x^n + y^n\), where \(n\) is a natural number?

Statement-I :

\(n\) is odd.

Statement-II :

\(n\) is even.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?

options.label: A
options.text: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other Statement alone

options.label: B
options.text: The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone

options.label: C
options.text: The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone

options.label: D
options.text: The Question can be answered even without using any of the Statements
